evidence: Cic. Tusc. 1.1: aut omnīnō aut magnā ex parte (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Also maximā ex parte, for the most part; aliquā ex parte, to some extent (see partly). For “mostly” of people and things counted, see most.

evidence: Caes. BG 4.1: maximam partem lacte atque pecore vīvunt (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Or. 189: magnam partem ex iambīs nostra cōnstat ōrātiō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The same idea in the accusative, common in Caesar and Livy (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: amō enim, quae maximā ex parte ipse incohāvī aut incohāta percoluī
phrases.english: for I love the things I largely began myself, or finished once they were begun

phrases.latin: maximam partem lacte atque pecore vīvunt
phrases.english: they live mainly on milk and meat

phrases.latin: magnam partem ex iambīs nostra cōnstat ōrātiō
phrases.english: our speech is made up largely of iambs
